call and they're both a little bit wrong

first place. And when you run the real

script.ending_words:
was
there. That's real, and no spreadsheet
gets to take it from him. But West
bought a decade, and when his kid asks a
different question, the boring one, the
one about whether they can actually

script.analysis: All 18,895 stored characters read in three contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Paired-character narrative: Danny (attends) versus Wes (invests the same $9,000), same age/city/job/$55K income/$9K savings. Early subscribe CTA after the hook. Danny arc: ticket status signaling, $60 headline price versus dynamic pricing and resale, flights across 16 host cities in three countries, tripled hotel rates, small costs, ~$9,000 total, financing via card/BNPL at 22%+, betting apps, home-viewer "quiet trap" (~$900 of streaming, bar tabs, bets), October statement. Wes arc: boring year one, year-two temptation and "closing the tab", 10% growth to ~$23K at 10 years and ~$60K at 20, repeated every-four-years scenario ~$150K+. Turn: experiential-purchase and anticipation research, unique home World Cup and son Leo, mega-event host returns negative, middle-path Danny (save cash, one match, one jersey). Close: countdown clocks serve the seller; "check the price, then choose". Notably balanced and story-driven, with recurring callbacks and an explicit counterargument. Uses a 10% nominal return without inflation or volatility; assumes Danny's entire savings spent each cycle. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:7000 2026 tournament across three countries and 16 host cities, 48 teams, group-stage tickets advertised from about $60 and variable/dynamic pricing are consistent with widely reported FIFA plans; not verified here against an official receipt. Host cities "more than 2,000 miles apart" plausible (e.g., Vancouver-Miami). 90,000-seat crowd plausible only for the largest venues. Hotel "triple" rates and Danny cost lines are illustrative, not sourced.

7000:14000 $9,000 at 10%: 10 years ~$23,344 ("low to mid 20,000s" correct), 20 years ~$60,547 (~$60K correct). Five $9,000 contributions at years 0,4,8,12,16 valued at year 20 = ~$162,600, consistent with "north of $150,000". Uses 10% nominal; at 7% the single-sum 20-year value is ~$34,800. Assumes no inflation adjustment and that Danny re-spends $9K every four years from a $9K savings base on a $55K income. 22% card APR consistent with prevailing averages. Betting "house always wins" is correct in expectation, not individually.

14000:18895 Experiential-purchase happiness research (e.g., Van Boven & Gilovich 2003) and anticipation effects (Kumar, Killingsworth & Gilovich 2014) are characterized broadly fairly, though "stubbornly consistent" overstates a literature with moderators. "First World Cup on North American soil since 1994" is literally correct (1994 USA was the last North American edition); first 48-team World Cup correct. Mega-event host return "-38%" attributed to one unnamed study; unverified. Host-city stadium cost-benefit skepticism matches mainstream sports-economics findings in general.

Timely but short shelf life; originality is high relative to generic frugality lists because of the balanced experience-value turn.
